display.title: Melave Malka: The Special Guest
display.summary_short: How the Alter Rebbe's script began on Rosh Chodesh Shevat, and how a hidden tzaddik's Melave Malka guest turned out to be Eliyahu HaNavi.
display.summary_long: For the week of Rosh Chodesh Shevat, the storyteller explains its anniversary: the Maggid of Mezritch asked the Alter Rebbe to design letters for sifrei Torah, tefillin and mezuzos that satisfy every opinion, and the new script was first used on Rosh Chodesh Shevat. Rabbi Zusha of Anipoli, told of it from Heaven, had the scribe Reb Moshe Sofer write his tefillin in it too. The story then follows that scribe when he was still a hidden tzaddik, working as the supervisor in Reb Yankel's whiskey factory. Every Motzaei Shabbos the two shared Melave Malka and spoke only words of Torah. Along the way the storyteller explains why Melave Malka matters: the Gemara's teaching, a warm dish, Miriam's well, Dovid HaMelech's thanksgiving meal and the luz bone. One week Reb Yankel is too busy, goes to find Moshe late at night, and sees a radiant old man at his table. Moshe admits it was Eliyahu HaNavi, who told him to reveal himself and become a teacher, and children announce the new Rebbe when he arrives.
display.lesson: Make Melave Malka every week, even a small bite, and go out of your way to help someone who needs it.
